title: Which NFL team has drafted the best since 2000?
text:
Although not entirely, the NFL draft plays an influential role in determining every team’s success each season. While teams can also build through free agency, the NFL draft helps determine how successful a team will be for the foreseeable future.
A great measure of the success of each individual draft pick is drafted approximate value (drAV). This means the value each draft pick provided to the team that drafted them. This helps determine how successful each individual draft pick was.
The first thing we will look at is every team’s accumulated drafted approximate value since 2000. This combines every draft from the last 25 years.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggrepel)

draft24 <- read_csv("2024draft.csv")
draft23 <- read_csv("2023draft.csv")
draft22 <- read_csv("2022draft.csv")
draft21 <- read_csv("2021draft.csv")
draft20 <- read_csv("2020draft.csv")
draft19 <- read_csv("2019draft.csv")
draft18 <- read_csv("2018draft.csv")
draft17 <- read_csv("2017draft.csv")
draft16 <- read_csv("2016draft.csv")
draft15 <- read_csv("2015draft.csv")
draft14 <- read_csv("2014draft.csv")
draft13 <- read_csv("2013draft.csv")
draft12 <- read_csv("2012draft.csv")
draft11 <- read_csv("2011draft.csv")
draft10 <- read_csv("2010draft.csv")
draft09 <- read_csv("2009draft.csv")
draft08 <- read_csv("2008draft.csv")
draft07 <- read_csv("2007draft.csv")
draft06 <- read_csv("2006draft.csv")
draft05 <- read_csv("2005draft.csv")
draft04 <- read_csv("2004draft.csv")
draft03 <- read_csv("2003draft.csv")
draft02 <- read_csv("2002draft.csv")
draft01 <- read_csv("2001draft.csv")
draft00 <- read_csv("2000draft.csv")

drafts <- bind_rows(draft00, draft01, draft02, draft03, draft04, draft05, draft06, draft07, draft08, draft09, draft10, draft11, draft12, draft13, draft14, draft15, draft16, draft17, draft18, draft19, draft20, draft21, draft22, draft23, draft24)

drafts <- drafts |>
  mutate(Tm = gsub("OAK", "LVR", Tm),
         Tm = gsub("STL", "LAR", Tm),
         Tm = gsub("SDG", "LAC", Tm))

drafts <- drafts |>
  mutate(Mascot = case_when(
    Tm == "ARI" ~ "Cardinals",
    Tm == "ATL" ~ "Falcons",
    Tm == "BAL" ~ "Ravens",
    Tm == "BUF" ~ "Bills",
    Tm == "CAR" ~ "Panthers",
    Tm == "CHI" ~ "Bears",
    Tm == "CIN" ~ "Bengals",
    Tm == "CLE" ~ "Browns",
    Tm == "DAL" ~ "Cowboys",
    Tm == "DEN" ~ "Broncos",
    Tm == "DET" ~ "Lions",
    Tm == "GNB"  ~ "Packers",
    Tm == "HOU" ~ "Texans",
    Tm == "IND" ~ "Colts",
    Tm == "JAX" ~ "Jaguars",
    Tm == "KAN"  ~ "Chiefs",
    Tm == "LVR"  ~ "Raiders",
    Tm == "LAC" ~ "Chargers",
    Tm == "LAR" ~ "Rams",
    Tm == "MIA" ~ "Dolphins",
    Tm == "MIN" ~ "Vikings",
    Tm == "NWE"  ~ "Patriots",
    Tm == "NOR"  ~ "Saints",
    Tm == "NYG" ~ "Giants",
    Tm == "NYJ" ~ "Jets",
    Tm == "PHI" ~ "Eagles",
    Tm == "PIT" ~ "Steelers",
    Tm == "SEA" ~ "Seahawks",
    Tm == "SFO"  ~ "49ers",
    Tm == "TAM"  ~ "Buccaneers",
    Tm == "TEN" ~ "Titans",
    Tm == "WAS" ~ "Commanders",
    TRUE ~ Tm
  ))

teamdrafts <- drafts |>
  group_by(Mascot) |>
  summarise(
    total_DrAV = sum(DrAV, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_games = sum(G, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_picks = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(total_DrAV))

top16drAV <- teamdrafts |>
  top_n(n = 16, wt = total_DrAV)

Greenbay <- top16drAV |>
  filter(Mascot == "Packers")

bar1 <- ggplot() +
  geom_bar(data=top16drAV, aes(x=reorder(Mascot, total_DrAV), weight=total_DrAV), fill="grey") +
  geom_bar(data=Greenbay, aes(x=reorder(Mascot, total_DrAV), weight=total_DrAV), fill="#FFB612") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Green Bay leads NFL in homegrown talent since 2000",
    subtitle = "Aaron Rodgers and David Bahktiari headline the Packers lead in drafted approximate value.",
    caption = "",
    x = "",
    y = "Approximate Value") +
  theme_minimal()+ 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 

bottom16drAV <- teamdrafts |>
  top_n(n = -16, wt = total_DrAV)

bar2 <- ggplot() + 
  geom_bar(data=bottom16drAV, aes(x=reorder(Mascot, total_DrAV), weight=total_DrAV), fill="grey") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 3000)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "",
    subtitle = "",
    caption = "Source: Pro Football Reference | By Cody Wagoner",
    x = "",
    y = "Approximate Value") +
  theme_minimal()+ 
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 8), 
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size=10), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
    ) 

bar1 + bar2









The Green Bay Packers come out on top, followed by the Pittsburgh Steelers, Baltimore Ravens, Dallas Cowboys, and New England Patriots. Each of these top five teams has sustained consistent success within the last 25 years, and it’s evident their success in the draft has played a factor.
However, without a talented offense, no points can be scored. Let’s now look at how every team performed when drafting on the offensive side of the ball.
This chart measures the accumulated rushing and receiving yards gained by draft picks of every team.
The Cincinnati Bengals lead here, followed closely by the Philadelphia Eagles.
Notice the Patriots dropping near the bottom after ranking top five in drafted approximate value. This could indicate they significantly used free agency to build their offensive skill positions.
